guide.title: Community Guidelines
x: reccos works because people trust each other’s reccos. These guidelines are part of our Terms of Use. They give examples, not a complete list. We may act on anything we reasonably think harms reccos or the people who use it.
Only recco places you’ve actually been to.
Give your real opinion. Loved, Fine and Didn’t Like are all fair game.
Don’t recco or rank a venue you own, work for or have a stake in, or a competitor of one.
Don’t buy, sell, swap or coordinate reccos, and don’t use extra accounts to push a place up or down.
Getting something free doesn’t change the rules: rank it honestly, and say so wherever reccos gives you the option.
Talk about the food, drink, service and place, not people’s looks, background or private lives.
Don’t name or single out venue staff in a negative way.
No harassment, threats, hate or bullying, including towards creators, venues and other users.
No sexually explicit, violent or illegal content.
Don’t post other people’s personal information.
Don’t post content you don’t have the rights to, such as other people’s photos or videos.
Stick to your own experience, and don’t make claims about a venue you can’t back up, such as about food safety or hygiene.
Don’t pretend to be someone else, or a creator, venue or brand.
No spam, ads or promotions we haven’t approved.
Report a user, a recco, a video or wrong venue details in the app, or email [contact email].
We review reports, and may also act without one. We may remove content, limit features, or suspend or close accounts that break these guidelines.
If we act on your content or account, you can ask us to review the decision by emailing [contact email].
We may update these guidelines at any time.
